status_note: Art. 6(1a), 1b, 1c inserted by 2026/1744 Art. 1 point (8); paraphrase matches official extraction. Art. 3(14) is amended by point (4)(a); its content was not read.

instrument: FAA Part 107 Waiver Section Specific Evaluation Information
status_note: FAA guidance document, no edition date seen
requirement_paraphrase: FAA waiver evaluators review the applicant's ConOps and hazard/risk analysis (severity, likelihood, mitigations, residual risk). For a 107.31 BVLOS waiver they check how the RPIC knows aircraft altitude/attitude/movement within C2-link limits, detects and avoids traffic, is alerted to degraded functionality, has the knowledge and skill, and which C2 links and FCC authorisations are used (BVLOS should not rely on FCC Part 5/15 devices). Under 107.25 (moving vehicle) lost-link behaviour must not create noncompliance. DAA evidence scales with risk: applicant statement and data (low), third-party validation plus an industry standard such as ASTM F3442 or RTCA DO-365 (medium), possible FAA/CAA certification (high).

instrument: Federal Decree-Law No. (26) of 2022 on civil use of unmanned aircraft
edition_or_version: Issued 26 Sep 2022 per UAE legislation portal
status_note: In force; Art. 29 says effect three months after publication; text partly OCR-garbled in fetch
requirement_paraphrase: Applies to all drones in the UAE incl. free zones except security-agency drones; GCAA and local authorities keep the registry and issue permits and certificates; owners must register drones before flight; many acts need authorisation (restricted-zone flights, cameras, modifications, trade/import/design/maintenance); a safety certificate is required before use; fines AED 50,000-500,000 for operating unregistered, reckless flying, no safety certificate, unapproved modification; AED 100,000-2,000,000 for unlicensed design/manufacture/trade/import; prison and fines for endangering airspace.
applies_to: Drone owners, operators, manufacturers, importers in UAE
